improvement.mechanism: Extend messaging-reliability with the atomic batch publication boundary. A successful single stream batch is committed in contiguous stream order, while consumer processing order and external effects still require their own guarantees. Chunk reconstruction needs identity, index, count and integrity metadata even when storage adjacency holds.
improvement.reading_and_contract_limits: The two articles were read completely, including examples and limitations, but the NATS server, clients and sample commands were not executed. Minimum versions, opt-in stream configuration, batch size, inactivity timeout, retry behavior and commit acknowledgement loss need deployed-version verification. The older article overstates simultaneous consumer delivery; the newer ordering article explicitly separates stream storage and processing.
improvement.discriminating_case: A batch commits, its acknowledgement is lost, and a subject-filtered consumer sees only a subset of chunks while another message is redelivered. Require reconciliation of the batch outcome and validation of complete logical payload identity. Do not infer processing order or business-effect atomicity from stream adjacency.
